title: Box-building chain: mixato, makelatticeato, randomise, fmole
purpose: Runs the complete EPSR box-building workflow [@epsrmanual] in sequence — mix molecules, replicate the box, randomise positions and orientations, relax the molecules — as a user would before starting `epsr` [@soper1996,@soper2005]. With a Linux `system_commands.txt`, every file prompt goes through the real directory listing.
system: A dimethyl sulphoxide-water mixture [@soperluzar1992] at 300 K: 4 DMSO + 8 water (64 atoms) at 0.1 atoms/Å³, cubic side 8.618 Å (`mixbox.ato`), replicated 2×2×2 to 96 molecules (32 DMSO + 64 water, 512 atoms) in a cubic box of 17.235 Å (`big.ato`), then randomised and shaken 10 times with the intramolecular Monte Carlo of `fmole` [@metropolis1953].
inputs: `DMSO.ato`, `WaterMolecule.ato` from EPSR-test; `system_commands.txt` (`system_ls ls`, `system_termination /`). `mixato.stdin` and `fmole.stdin` answer each listing prompt with `e` and a typed name (independent of the `ls` sort order). Commands: `mixato < mixato.stdin`, `makelatticeato mixbox 2 2 2 big n`, `randomise big`, `fmole < fmole.stdin` (`big`, 10 shakes).
verification: Four program calls in one pass, each consuming the previous output, so the random-number state is carried through `randomise` and `fmole`. Compared outputs: `mixbox.ato`, `big.ato` and `dirlist.txt` (the listing `./DMSO.ato`, `./WaterMolecule.ato`, `./big.ato`, `./mixbox.ato`), all identical.
